proposals.rationale: The published template log-analytics-pipeline@1 declares decomposition.children = [parse-log-events, render-stats-report, aggregate-event-stats] with no dependency edges, and the runtime admits the batch's children one at a time in exactly that declared recipe order (decompose result: "starts the children one at a time in dependency order"; observed schedule parse -> report -> aggregate). render-stats-report's own contract hard-gates on out/stats.json existing and being newer than out/events.json, which can only hold after aggregate-event-stats has run, so on every fresh checkout the report stage is admitted before its producer and must fail. The template objective compounds this by ordering the children "parse, report and aggregate" in one sentence while demanding "respect their data dependency order" in the same paragraph. The repair is internal to the template: declare the children in their only valid data order (parse-log-events -> aggregate-event-stats -> render-stats-report) and make the objective name that same order, leaving contract criteria, caps and child template digests untouched.

appliesTo: Own and independently verify the parse, aggregate and report stages of the log-analytics pipeline.

contract.objective: Own the log-analytics pipeline: parse.mjs, aggregate.mjs and report.mjs must exist in the checkout root and running them in order (`node parse.mjs events.log`, `node aggregate.mjs`, `node report.mjs`) must produce out/events.json, out/stats.json and out/report.md accepted by the independent checker. Coordinate the three stages as independently verified children in their data dependency order — parse, then aggregate, then report — and reuse the available stage templates where applicable. Begin by expanding this contract's own recipe: call task_decompose with this template's exact templateRef at the top level and no reason or children, so the runtime binds the parse, aggregate and report children in the recipe's data order. Never author a stage contract inline, copy a stage objective by hand, or repair a stage template from here.

gate.targetFailureFixed: Yes. The frozen two-sided experiment (exp-334c9b47c48ef99c, repetition 0, candidate log-analytics-pipeline@2 sha256:11fb33c9f172cffe2b49296ed4e86302f2666c546cc2ddc5f0db80076d245bfc) reports verdict "fixed": on the observed failure t-6d4d7f94-bdd9-4891-b62c-d3263e7d1261 the freshly started baseline side failed pipeline-result while the candidate side passed (fail→pass). Mechanism matches the diagnosis: the recipe now lists parse-log-events → aggregate-event-stats → render-stats-report, so render-stats-report is admitted only after aggregate-event-stats wrote out/stats.json, and the objective no longer orders the children "parse, report, aggregate".
gate.originalAcceptanceMaintained: Yes. The candidate template's contract is byte-identical in acceptance to log-analytics-pipeline@1: the single deterministic mandatory criterion pipeline-result `node checks/verify.mjs pipeline` with protected inputs checks/verify.mjs and events.log (sha256 34b122631fa3ff208b33bb3833303719bde66ee1853ec7614f9b4214961c6612 and be0ecc6e412583229d9976bbc8f6c81e644b8b88b3290cea37517aaa0ad8d958), plus the unchanged constraints. The candidate side passed that original independent oracle in the experiment.
gate.existingRegressionMaintained: Yes. Both frozen holdouts were verified on both sides with no criterion diff in the experiment: t-830e50d4-5b96-4423-a4f5-6b2fdadedc8b (parse-log-events, evidence-r-6ce4b036-9719-4dd3-84b8-a9f313d99278-a3fef138-2af2-4c65-b2b3-e8c04fb2bfa9) and t-be201508-7727-4733-a77a-6d3c4ea18d3d (aggregate-event-stats, evidence-r-2daaec9a-618a-41b0-9ab6-2753ece2d96d-3f931884-31ff-4aa6-ae6d-bb4b1b31fb20). The three child stage templates and their digests are unchanged, so per-stage checks verify.mjs parse|aggregate|report are unaffected.
gate.noUnacceptableSideEffects: Yes. Only decomposition.children order, decomposition.reason and the objective sentence that named the child order changed; the only published template mutated is log-analytics-pipeline (child templates parse-log-events@1, aggregate-event-stats@1, render-stats-report@1 are carried at their existing digests and untouched). No capability, tool, provider or protected input is changed, and events.log and checks/verify.mjs stay untouched (unchanged constraint). Existing admitted Tasks and frozen Runs keep their recorded definitions.
gate.holdoutPerformanceAcceptable: Yes. Nonempty holdout set: the two verified sibling stages t-830e50d4 and t-be201508, each still verified under the candidate with no criterion diff, and the candidate side passed the pipeline acceptance that the baseline side failed.
gate.resourceCostAcceptable: Yes. The experiment ran one baseline and one candidate side for the failed parent plus a baseline/candidate pair per holdout under the deployment's own runtime limits with no maxTokens ceiling declared; the candidate removes a guaranteed-to-fail report stage admission and its wasted run rather than adding work, so cost per attempt does not grow.
